note: Presets are saved parameter sets for the same animation; they do not count as additional animations. All content is fictional and illustrative (jurisdiction unspecified). A (reference scenario, ●) and B (alleged loss, ◆) are identical machines with equal weight; the only difference is B's open ◆ gate, which lets out the supplied stated difference. Every amount is a fictional figure shown as supplied; nothing is computed, valued or decided and no winner, damages, compensation, liability, fault or causation conclusion is drawn. Long-labels-stress: coordinator decision (standing stress-cap rule, docs/AUTHORING.md item 20, from LAW-0687/0689–0692; subject floor: 'Subject ≥ 0.20 of the frame height at rest and hold (causation-05 LAW-0700 decision)', production/SESSION_HANDOFF.md). True driver: the 1:1 and 9:16 boxes (each machine must reach 0.20 of the frame height with both scenes shown). After trying the fallback layouts (A and B side by side; stacked with the shared entries under them, in one or two columns; stacked beside a right-hand text column, with the late chips under the lanes; heads beside the hoppers), the full stress counts did not fit 1:1 without the fallback scale. Measured, rendered at 1080p (2026-09-27): full counts (five entries, two alternatives, two labelled links, two stated items, two shared facts) → 1:1 fallback scale k 0.714, smallest text 12.1 px, machines 0.080 of the frame height; 9:16 18.0 px / 0.186; 16:9 20.0 px / 0.242. The stress keeps every text at its near-maximum length and caps the COUNTS at four entries, no alternative, no link note, one stated item and one shared fact (baseline 3 / 0 / 0 / 1 / 1); after the cap: 1:1 17.0 px / 0.258 without scaling; 9:16 20.0 px / 0.213; 16:9 22.0 px / 0.342. Every field stays longer than the baseline and every count ≥ the baseline.
